scope: Repair all active protected Preview browser QA entrypoints with one redirect-safe credential handler; verify private source exposure using ordinary protected navigation and correct the Linux executable-mode test fixture.
riskAnalysis: Playwright browser header overrides survive redirects. Keep credentials on a separate exact-origin non-following fetch, fulfill its response, and allow native browser redirects without global credentials. Preserve private response-body confidentiality and all source/owner/controller boundaries. This changes QA access transport, not provider inference authorization.

threatModel.assets: Preview protection and QA/bootstrap credentials, private repository source, immutable release identity and authenticated browser evidence.
threatModel.trustBoundaries: Protected Preview origin versus arbitrary foreign redirects; Node API request versus browser request; private source route versus public assets.
threatModel.abuseCases: Foreign redirect forwarding custom credentials, global headers on third-party assets, false private-source pass from login/protection failures, leaked raw request exception, executable-mode test falsely accepting mutation.
threatModel.mitigations: Shared exact-origin route.fetch with maxRedirects zero followed by fulfill; no global headers; off-origin removal of all four existing private header types; positive public200 and exact-origin/path404 private probes with no body read; fixed diagnostic messages; actual Git mode-change assertion.

defects.rootCause: Browser route.continue header overrides are inherited by foreign redirects. Existing separate-origin filtering is bypassed for redirected requests.
defects.detectionGap: Pure URL/header tests did not exercise an actual native browser redirect. Independent two-origin local Chrome fixture with fictional credentials proved forwarding.
defects.regression: Actual imported-handler Chrome redirect/cookie fixture plus tests for no global credentials, maxRedirects zero, off-origin filtering and every active caller migration.
defects.historicalPrevention: All four browser QA entrypoints use the same helper; retain original fixture proof and failed hosted browser evidence, with no claim that any real credential was exposed.

defects.rootCause: New private-source probe disabled redirects before protection cookie bootstrap; exact original response status was not preserved. Linux mode test staged chmod was canceled by worktree mode tracking.
defects.detectionGap: The private probe did not use the same ordinary navigation as authenticated UI, and local Windows mode semantics did not match Linux.
defects.regression: Positive public200/private404 normal navigation, foreign/path/login/error denial; mode fixture disables worktree mode tracking and verifies100644-to100755 raw diff before guard rejection.
defects.historicalPrevention: Keep runtime formatting guard unchanged and preserve the original5368-of5369 CI result; fixtures assert their own filesystem/Git preconditions.

rollback: Keep paid execution disabled and preserve all failed/successful receipts. If qualification fails, retain the current feature alias or restore the preceding qualified feature deployment; never mutate main or Production.

negativePaths.malformed-response: Unexpected private response status, URL, path, absent response or navigation exception fails with fixed probe/status diagnostics and no body or raw URL.
negativePaths.stale-state: Exact source, release pin and private-source identity unchanged; new hosted Browser artifacts must match the actual successor before any paid Chief operation.
negativePaths.concurrency: Existing Browser workflow concurrency remains single per feature branch; this helper grants no concurrent provider execution or mutation rights.
negativePaths.cancellation: Browser context closure and existing workflow cancellation terminate pending fetches; bounded30second transport timeout retained, no automatic retry.
negativePaths.worker-interruption: Navigation/fetch failures abort browser request and retain fixed diagnostics; no success inferred from an interrupted fixture or missing screenshot.
negativePaths.api-outage: HTTP401/403/200 at private paths cannot masquerade as private404; public positive control must200, all probes same-origin and exact path.
negativePaths.authorization-denial: Private header types stripped off-origin; same-origin separate fetch cannot follow redirects; browser carries no global custom credential headers.
negativePaths.spending-limit: No OpenAI or Sandbox requests in local security tests; owner-directed existing financial monitoring and uncertainty unchanged; no new paid resources.
negativePaths.partial-execution: Prior CI/Browser failures preserved; no paid Chief task is authorized until every required hosted check and artifact inspection passes.

proactiveReview.architecture: One shared existing QA access helper covers every active entrypoint; normal private-source browser navigation uses that transport, no new orchestration or credential system.
proactiveReview.dependencies: Existing Playwright browser and Node APIs only, no packages or providers added. Actual proof uses isolated localhost fictional credentials, not personal browser state.
proactiveReview.threats: Cross-origin redirect forwarding is demonstrated with fictional credentials and eliminated by separate non-following request/fulfill, not by disabling protection.
proactiveReview.failureModes: Lost responses and raw transport exceptions fail closed; positive control excludes generic404/login false positives, mode fixture verifies its actual staged condition.
proactiveReview.faultInjection: Foreign redirects, cookie bootstrap, private200/403, foreign404, wrong path, malformed response, raw error containing a fictional secret and executable-mode mutation.
proactiveReview.independentChallenge: Existing independent Work QA exercises actual imported helper in real headless browser; Engineering Auditor separately reviews every active caller and diagnostics.
proactiveReview.recovery: Preserve current66c and original failed artifacts; one reviewed feature source push/build, durable alias marker/readback once READY, no configuration refresh or credential rewrite.
proactiveReview.readiness: Fifteen focused tests passed. Final independent actual-browser proof and source-bound hosted CI, Redis, CodeQL, Jekyll and authenticated Browser artifact qualification required before paid Chief discovery.
